entries.title: Safety-shell structure
entries.summary: Pre-snap and post-snap safety structure is evidence used to narrow possible coverage families; the initial picture can be disguised and must not be treated as the final coverage.
principles: Compare pre-snap alignment with post-snap rotation.
limitations: Shell alone does not uniquely identify coverage.
Modern match coverages and disguise can make static labels misleading.
fantasyImplications: Potential input to matchup analysis only after team/player performance versus structures is measured and validated.

provenance.note: Foundational football concept; authoritative source set to be attached during library sourcing pass.

entries.title: Motion as diagnostic evidence
entries.summary: Pre-snap motion can force defensive communication or adjustment and provide evidence about responsibility, leverage and coverage structure.
principles: Observe whether a defender travels, bumps or exchanges responsibility.
Observe safety, nickel and linebacker responses to motion.
Use the response as evidence, not as a one-signal coverage declaration.
limitations: A traveling defender does not prove pure man coverage.
Match rules and disguise can mimic man/zone tells.
fantasyImplications: Hypothesis: offenses/players that exploit motion-created information may have matchup-specific advantages versus defenses whose preferred structures are exposed or stressed by motion.

provenance.note: Former Z/slot receiver: safety alignment and defensive movement in response to frequent pre-snap motion were primary tells.

entries.title: Offense-defense scheme interaction improves fantasy matchup evaluation
entries.summary: Fantasy matchup quality may improve when SAGE measures how an offense/player performs against the coverage structures an opponent actually uses, rather than relying primarily on aggregate fantasy points allowed.
principles: Measure defensive usage percentages by structure.
Measure offensive and player efficiency/opportunity against the same structures.
Intersect tendency, performance, role and sample confidence.
limitations: Early samples can be distorted by opponent quality, injuries, game state and quarterback quality.
fantasyImplications: Candidate input for Weekly SAGE matchup adjustments after backtesting.
